newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close sharply lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close sharply lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower on Tuesday after heavy profit-taking undid 200 points of initial gains, brokers said.
"There is overseas concern about the property market and that is the main drag. Of course, Telecom is (also) the main leader downward," said Steven Thompson, chief analyst at Nikko Securities.
The Hang Seng Index dropped 215.42 points, or 1.47 percent, to finish at 14,439.71 after retreating from an early high of 14,856.77.
Turnover was a hefty HK$20.91 billion, slightly lower than Friday's HK$21.69 billion. The market was closed on Monday.
"Foreign investors unloaded their holdings in the market, which is undergoing a downdard price adjustment after the recent sharp rise," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
The market would be healthier if the Hang Seng could move down towards the 14,000 level, Lai said.
Hongkong Telecom bore the brunt of the selling, dropping HK$1.65 to close at HK$17.35 on volume of 141.49 million shares worth HK$2.54 billion.
Analysts said investors took profit on Hongkong Telecom following news that Cable & Wireless agreed to sell part of its stake to China Telecom.
"The deal is positive since Hongkong Telecom will see a new market in China," said Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House.
Blue chip properties fell on fears the government would announce new measures to cool speculation in the local property market, brokers said.
Cheung Kong eased HK$1.25 to HK$75.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped HK$2.25 at HK$90.50.
HSBC rose HK$2.00 to HK$230.00 after touching a new high of HK$236.00. Bank of East Asia was up HK$0.20 to HK$29.25.
Sentiment on red chips was hit by China's recent drive to curb speculation on China's stock markets, brokers said.
Beijing Enterprises dropped HK$3.25 to HK$47.00, Shanghai Industrial fell HK$1.90 to HK$41.50 and Guangdong Investment was down HK$0.25 at HK$9.50.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprise Index shed 23.09 points, or 2.19 percent, to 1,032.47.
